spatial_claims.claim: A is on semicircle BAC with diameter BC; E is the centre of the circle, lying on BC
EB = EA (radii), so triangle ABE is isosceles
EA = EC (radii), so triangle AEC is isosceles
angle BAC = angle EAB + angle EAC: ray AE falls between rays AB and AC (E is between B and C on segment BC)
In triangle ABC, angles sum to two right angles
For chord AC (not diameter), the segment containing the centre is the greater segment
B in greater segment implies arc ADC is the minor arc
Inscribed angle ABC subtends minor arc ADC; central angle on minor arc < two right angles
Diameter AD drawn through centre from A passes through interior of greater segment
angle DAC claimed to equal a right angle by semicircle theorem (misapplication: A is endpoint of diameter AD, not on the arc)
Angle of lesser segment at A is contained within the angle of the semicircle at A

configuration_map: Circle with centre E (or O). Diameter BC with E as midpoint. Point A on semicircle BAC. Ray AE from A to centre E falls between rays AB and AC because E lies between B and C on segment BC -- this validates the angle decomposition in Step 4. For the greater/lesser segment part: chord AC divides circle into major arc (containing B, the greater segment) and minor arc (containing D, the lesser segment). The centre lies in the greater segment. Inscribed angle at B subtends minor arc, inscribed angle at D subtends major arc. In Step 21, a diameter AD is drawn from A through the centre; this diameter passes through the greater segment's interior since it contains the centre. All point positions are mutually consistent throughout the proof.
pass_reason: All spatial claims (point positions, angle decompositions, arc classifications) are mutually consistent. The Step 4 angle decomposition (angle BAC = angle EAB + angle EAC) is valid because E lies between B and C on the diameter, so ray AE falls between rays AB and AC. The arc and inscribed angle reasoning in Steps 18-19 is spatially sound. The issues in Steps 20-22 (claiming angle DAC is a right angle by the semicircle theorem when A is an endpoint of the diameter, not a point on the arc) are theorem misapplications (logical errors in citation), not spatial configuration contradictions -- the underlying point positions remain consistent.
